entries: Pie and donut charts: a click on a slice now shows its details. Each `PieSeries` sets `selectable: true`; without it Qt Graphs emits no `clicked` signal. The 2-level pies of Account Details are one `GraphsView` with two `PieSeries` again, and the ring and the slice of a click come from the position of the press, because the Qt Graphs 6.10 hit test ignores `holeSize`. The subcategory ring starts 0.03 outside the category ring, as intended, instead of under it (#57).

Overview, net worth chart: the hover lines on the layer borders are no longer drawn in the green of the theme. They have the colour of their layer, and so have the markers and the tooltip titles (#58).

Bar charts: the hover tooltip of every bar is shown in full. Before, the tooltip of a stacked segment was drawn under the segments above it, and the tooltip of the tallest bars was cut at the top of the chart. `HoverBar` shows a `ToolTip`, drawn in the overlay of the window (#59).

Account Details, balance chart: the Y-axis "Auto" / "From 0" toggle now changes the axis. "Auto" fits the axis to the balances (10 % of the range on each side); before, it started at 0 for an account that is never negative, as "From 0" does. "From 0" includes 0: it starts the axis at 0 for a positive account and ends it at 0 for a negative account. An account that is always negative now shows its line with both settings (#65).

Import Transactions: a visit to another page during a review no longer loses it. The page is loaded the first time it is shown and is then kept; "Done" on the import report starts the next import at step 1. The target account is kept by its id, so an account added or removed on another page meanwhile does not change the account that Save writes to (#64).

Manage Accounts, account dialog: an edit keeps a currency that is not in the list, instead of saving EUR. A type, category or currency that is not in its list (removed, or unknown) is shown in its box as "<value> (kept)", and Save keeps it; an empty category shows "(none)" (#63).

Import review and account Transactions tables: every column can be reached at the default window size (1280 px). Before, the RULE and KEEP columns of the import review and the Edit button of the Transactions table were cut off. The header and the rows scroll horizontally when the columns are wider than the card, with a visible scroll bar, and fill the card when it is wider. The column-width handles of the import review still drag in the scroll area (#60, #61).

Requirement check (`tools/check-requirements.sh` / `.ps1`): a `QT_VERSION` below 6.10 now fails, as `CMakeLists.txt` requires (`qt_standard_project_setup(REQUIRES 6.10)`). Before, 6.8 and 6.9 passed the check, and the Docker build then stopped at configure. `README.md`, `CI-CD.md` and `ci.yml` now say Qt 6.10+ (#81).

qmllint: the project target (`FinanceDashboard_qmllint`) reports no warning (21 before). `ImportSnapshotPage.qml` and `InvestmentsPage.qml` declare `pragma ComponentBehavior: Bound`, the sidebar delegate of `Main.qml` reads its `modelData` through its id and sizes its line with `Layout.preferredHeight`, and the checkpoint list of Manage Accounts no longer uses a comma expression (#70).

Projects: the number fields read French input ("3,5", "40 000") and refuse anything else with a message. Before, "3,5" was read as 3, "40 000" as 40 and "40k" as 40, without a message. The New project dialog stays open and tells which value is wrong, also for a target of 0 or a month count outside 1 to 1200, which closed it with no project before (`addProject()` now returns whether it added the project). After an edit, the loan-rate field shows the rate that applies, and it follows the rate when it changes (#75, #66).

Database Management: "Delete account" deletes the account that its dialog names. Before, it deleted the account at the same position in the list, so another account when the list changed while the dialog was open. The two clean-up dialogs keep the account id, and they open only for a valid account (with no account, they threw a TypeError). Import: "Choose file & Import" is disabled when no statement template exists (#67, #68).

README.md: the Run and Tests steps work on Windows (the Qt `bin` folder on `PATH`, and `ctest -C Release` with the Visual Studio generator), with a Linux test example. The Docker section gives the bash options next to the PowerShell ones, says that a static build is still the launcher, `app/` and `app/requirements.txt`, and lists the system libraries that a Linux build needs. The project layout describes the tests folder as it is (#104, #94).

ARCHITECTURE.MD is a standalone document: no `docs/` folder and no dead link (#102). It adds a directory map, the steps to add a page, and the known Qt Graphs behaviour of this project (from the deleted `docs/charting-gotchas.md`, updated with #57, #58 and #59). Its rules are in ASD-STE100 (short sentences, one instruction each, no semicolons): `ste-lint.py` finds no hard violation (19 before) (#105).

releases.title: Import and calculations
releases.summary: Import and calculations release. Amounts are rounded to the cent, and the reconciliation adds whole cents. An account hash belongs to one account, and an 8- or 11-character BIC gives one hash. The category suggestions are the same in every run, short merchant names keep their own key, the stored rules follow the new keys, and the app computes the suggestions in a worker thread. Also includes fixes of the statement import, renames that reach every row, a Reset Database that stays empty, status colors, and the Test app with its pre-release channels and the update from inside the app.

entries: A Test app, "Finance Dashboard Test" (`cmake -DFD_APP_IDENTITY=test`), for the experimental and preprod builds. It installs and runs next to the prod app, with its own data folder and settings, its own Windows setup identity (AppId, install folder, Start menu folder, uninstall entry) and Linux desktop entry, an icon with an orange "TEST" band, and "(Test)" in the window title. The title of the start-up error window ends with the name of the app: "Can't start — Finance Dashboard" (before, "Finance Dashboard — can't start"). Its packages are the Windows setup and ZIP, and the AppImage. CI builds them, tests that the two Windows setups install side by side and uninstall one at a time, and checks that the Test AppImage keeps its data in its own folder (#130).

The Test app: "Copy my prod database" on the Database Management page replaces the Test data with a copy of the prod database, after a confirmation, so that a new version and its database upgrade can be tried on the real data. The prod database is only read (SQLite can leave its -wal and -shm files next to it). The Test data from before is kept in a file next to the Test database. An older copy is upgraded, with its backup copy and the upgrade report. A copy with a newer schema is refused, and a copy that does not open is kept while the Test data comes back. The Test database is not replaced while another window of the Test app uses it. The page scrolls when it is higher than the window (#130).

Release channels: CI publishes the Test app as GitHub pre-releases. Each push to develop, and each run of a pull request with the label "experimental", publishes an experimental build (v0.2.2-exp.<run>, v0.2.2-exp.<run>.pr<number>); each push to a release branch publishes a release candidate (v0.2.2-rc.<run>). <run> is the run number of the CI workflow, so the versions of a channel sort in build order. The version suffix goes into the version of the app, the setup and the file names. CI keeps the 10 newest experimental pre-releases, and the release of a version deletes its release candidates (#129).

Updates: at each start, the app asks GitHub for the list of releases and tells in a banner when a newer version of its channel exists. The new Updates page (ADMIN) shows the version of the app, the versions of the channel with their notes and release pages, a "Check now" button and the setting that turns the check off. The prod app follows the releases; the Test app follows Experimental (-exp and -rc) or Preprod (-rc). "Install" (in the banner or on the page) installs the newest version: the app downloads it from GitHub, with SHA256SUMS.txt, and checks its SHA-256. With the setup, "Install and restart" then runs the setup with a progress window: the setup closes the app, installs the new version and opens it (a copy "for all users" asks for administrator rights first). With the AppImage, the app replaces its file, and "Restart now" opens the new version. Nothing is downloaded or restarted without a click. The portable ZIP, the .deb and the .tar.gz update by hand: the page gives the steps. GitHub sees the internet address of the computer and the version of the app: the app sends no token, no cookie and no data, and English as the language. Without a network, when GitHub does not answer in time, or when GitHub refuses the call, the page tells why. The QML engine loads nothing from the network, the notes of a version are shown without their images, and the page opens the pages of the project on GitHub only. The check and the download use HTTPS: CI checks that the packages have the TLS backend of Qt, and on Linux they use the OpenSSL 3 of the system (the .deb depends on libssl3t64 | libssl3 and ca-certificates). CI also checks that the setup closes the running app, updates it and starts it again, in both install modes. The Docker build ships the TLS plugins and builds its static Linux Qt with OpenSSL (#117).
The Git history on GitHub was rewritten on 2026-10-20 at 06:39 UTC to remove personal data. A clone made before that time still has the old history: delete it and clone the repository again.

Release flow: when a `release/x.y.z` branch is pushed, CI opens a pull request that opens the next version on `develop` (`version.py cut`), so `develop` takes changes again while the release branch is tested; `version.py uncut` undoes it when a release branch is dropped. On `develop`, the version of the release branch stays undated ("release in progress"); the release branch dates it just before its merge into `main`. The back-merge is now a merge of `main` into a branch from `develop`, made by `tools/release_flow.py`, which renders `version.md` again when it conflicts. The Changelog job runs the new tests of the tools (`tools/test_version.py`). It refuses a pull request into `main` with an undated version, and a pull request into `develop` that changes the version of a release branch, or that comes before the pull request that opens the next version or before the back-merge. `CONTRIBUTING.md` tells when a whole stack can be merged at once (#131).
Statement import: the "Prénom Nom" line gives the account holder name again. The accent in the code was read as two Latin-1 characters, so the name was always "—" (#43).

Statement import: when the amount of the start balance line cannot be read, the end balance line no longer becomes the start balance, and the reconciliation no longer counts the unread balance as 0: no false gap and no adjustment row (#44).

Statement import: a CSV file saved as Windows-1252 (for example by a spreadsheet) is read. Before, "€" and the accented letters broke the balances and the holder name. A UTF-8 file with a few bad bytes stays UTF-8 (the bad bytes show as "�"), and a UTF-16 file with a byte order mark is read. The import log warns in each case. If you imported a Windows-1252 file before, a new import of the same file can add its rows that have no bank reference again: their description changed (#45).

Statement import: the reference block of a description is the run of reference lines at its end ("Internal ref.: …", "End-to-end ref.: …"). So a "ref" in the free text ("Rent for March, ref: APT12") stays in the transaction name, and a description with only reference lines gets its first line as the name instead of an empty name. Rows saved before keep their name (#46).

Status messages: a failure shows in red and a warning in amber, no longer in green, and a failure stays until the next message. A new message stays for the whole delay: one timer for each page controller, instead of one timer for each message (#54).
Import: when the save fails, the page stays on the review step with a red message. "Import another file" no longer shows the report of the earlier import (#39).
Import: "Auto-filled N of M" counts only the rows whose category the predictor filled, not the categories picked by hand. A subcategory picked by hand keeps the row in the count (#53).

A rename of a category, a subcategory, an account type or an account category now reaches the transactions, the category rules and the accounts that use the name, in one SQL transaction. Before, they kept the old name and lost their colour, and the predictor kept the old name. A rename to a name that exists (in any case) is refused with a message, and the Account Types & Categories page now shows the status messages (#34).

A null text from C++ in an optional column (the type, the category and the notes of an account, the note of a balance checkpoint) is now written as an empty string. Before, it failed the write with "NOT NULL constraint failed". The database now refuses an empty name, currency, account hash or hash source, and an invalid checkpoint date, before any write, with a message (#125).

"Reset Database" now stays empty: the default categories, account types, account categories and demo accounts no longer come back at the next start, or when a page opens after the reset. A new settings table of the database records that its defaults were written. The defaults and this record are written in one SQL transaction: if a write fails, nothing is written, and the next start tries again. The upgrade to schema version 3 records the defaults of a database that has data: the category defaults when it has categories, the account defaults when it has accounts, account types or account categories. A database that a reset emptied before this version gets the defaults one more time, at the first start after the upgrade: reset it again to empty it. After the upgrade, v0.2.1 cannot open the database ("a newer version of the app saved the file"); it can open the copy that the upgrade saves next to the file (#37).

"Reset to Mock Data" now writes the sample transactions: the code looked for the demo account by a name with an em dash in QLatin1String, which never matched. A write that fails now shows an error instead of a success (#38).

Accounts: after "Reset Database", "Add" in the account dialog saves the account without a type, and the dialog tells that there is no account type. Before, nothing happened: the empty list of types gave a TypeError. An edit of an account whose type or category is not in the list keeps it, instead of giving it the first type (#62).

Account History: the balance replays the transactions in booking order (the confirmation date), the order of the bank's own balance. A card payment made before the statement start and booked after it no longer moves the start of the line: the current balance is right (#36).

Projects page: with no monthly contribution, "Projected Completion" says "Never" instead of the current month, and the save-vs-borrow text no longer says "~0 more months". With no gap, the text says that there is no gap, instead of the gap of a 10 000 € sample loan (the loan scenarios still borrow that sample amount). "Still Needed" is 0, not a negative amount, when the earmarked amount is above the target. A contribution below half a cent counts as none, a completion after 100 years shows "Never", and a new project with an amount that is not a number or a target date after 100 years is refused (#41).

Cash Flow page (mock data): in a month where the spending is more than the income, the money flow gets an "Overspend" input (taken from the savings), so its two sides have the same total. Before, the savings output went to 0, and the outputs were more than the inputs (#42).
Cash Flow page (mock data): the 3-month average line starts at the third month. Before, its first two points were the averages of one and two months (#56).
Investments page (mock data): the monthly performance leaves out the deposit of the month. Before, the 250 € deposit counted as a gain: the second month showed 4.95 % instead of 2.48 % (#56).

Money: an amount is rounded to cents before its sign is set, so a very small negative value shows "0,00 €", not "-0,00 €". NaN and an infinity show "—" (before, they reached a conversion with undefined behaviour). The pages of one account (transactions, balance checkpoints, balance history and its chart, category totals) show the amounts of a USD account in $, not in €; the other pages keep the currency of the app (#48).

Database: a failed BEGIN or COMMIT is no longer ignored. "Reset Database", the save of a snapshot and the removal of a category or an account fail with a message when their SQL transaction cannot start or commit. Before, a failed commit counted as a success, and a reset without its transaction committed each table drop on its own. The table classes check that each statement is prepared and log the error of SQLite, instead of a misleading "Parameter count mismatch". The results of the WAL, secure_delete and checkpoint PRAGMAs are logged (#49).
Windows: `FinanceDashboard.exe` has its icon (Explorer, the shortcuts, the taskbar), and the window shows the app icon on Windows and Linux. Before, only the setup had the icon (#111).

Import: the start check of the reconciliation takes the last saved row in booking order (the confirmation date, else the operation date), as the balance history does. Before, it took the row with the latest operation date: a card payment made before the start of a statement but booked after it gave a false gap (#133).

Amounts: the reconciliation of an import compares whole cents, so a gap of one cent is a gap. Before, it compared doubles with a tolerance of 0.01: start 0.00, 0.10 and 0.20 in, 0.31 declared at the end gave "End balance OK". The adjustment row is the exact gap, and the import report, the balance history and the category totals add whole cents too. The app rounds each amount to the cent before it writes it, and the upgrade to schema version 4 rounds the stored amounts (the upgrade message tells how many rows changed; the copy from before the upgrade keeps the old values). An amount that is not a number or is larger than 10^13 is refused: in a statement, in the transaction and checkpoint dialogs, and in the database (#33).

Account hashes: a hash belongs to one account, and it is stored in lower case. The import suggests the account that has the hash of the statement. When you save the statement to another account (or click "Link this account"), the hash moves to that account, and the next import suggests it; the review screen tells it before the save. Before, a hash typed in upper case was not found (the save added a second link), and after one wrong link the import kept suggesting the first account. A typed hash must be 64 hexadecimal characters that no other account has: the message names that account. The upgrade to schema version 5 keeps the most recent link of each hash and tells how many links it removed (#47).

Account hashes: the BIC is used on 11 characters, so an 8-character BIC (`PSSTFRPP`) and the same BIC on 11 characters (`PSSTFRPPXXX`) give one hash. Before, a change of the export format unlinked the account, and the import no longer suggested it. The app keeps no IBAN or BIC, so it cannot compute the stored hashes again: the import also tries the hash of an 8-character BIC from before this change, and the save (or "Link this account") replaces it with the new one. When another account has that old hash, the review screen tells it before the save. The header of `AccountHashing.h` tells what the hash is for (the grouping of the statements of one account, and the suggestion) and its limit: it is not a security feature. The comments and the Accounts page no longer call the decision not to keep account numbers a "security decision" (#50).

Category prediction: the same data gives the same suggestion in every run. Before, a tie (as many "Transport" as "Leisure" rows for "SNCF CONNECT", two known labels equally close, equal neighbours) went to the label that the hash order of the run gave first, so the suggestion could change at each start. Now a tie goes to the label of the most recent row, in every rung of the predictor, and two rules of the same rank that both match give the category of the rule made last (#51).

Category prediction: short merchant names keep their own key. "Card payment 1234: H&M", "C&A", "AS24" and "O2" all gave the key "CARD PAYMENT", so they shared their suggestions and their rules: after two H&M rows in "Shopping / Clothes", AS24 (fuel) and O2 (telecom) got "Shopping / Clothes" in green. A label with only generic words ("VIREMENT EN VOTRE FAVEUR") now gets no key: no suggestion, and no rule. A reference ("Internal ref.: …", a UUID) is not a name either. The upgrade to schema version 6 normalizes the patterns of the stored category rules again: a rule whose label had only generic words (such as "CARD PAYMENT") is removed; rules that get one label merge into the newer one when they give one category, and are removed when they give different categories ("TRANSFER TO JOHN DOE" for the rent and "RECEIVED FROM JOHN DOE" for a refund are both "JOHN DOE" now, and one rule cannot give two categories). The upgrade message tells how many. Note: a key has no direction words now, so a rule covers both directions of a transfer (a rule for "Transfer to JOHN DOE" also applies to "Payment received from JOHN DOE"): check the suggestions for the transfers from a person who has a rule (#40).

Category prediction: ligatures are folded ("CŒUR BŒUF" is "COEUR BOEUF"), and month names ("MARS CARREFOUR", "RENT MARCH"), masked card numbers ("XXXXXXXXXXXX4972") and the English boilerplate of the Sumeria export ("Payment received from", "Transfer to", "Direct debit") are no longer part of the merchant key. A month name stays the name of a label that has no other one ("MARS", "APRIL"), and a month next to a day or a year ("05 MARS", "MARS 2026") is a date. Before, "RECEIVED FROM JOHN DOE" was close enough to "…JOHN SMITH" to get its category (#55).

Import: the category suggestions are computed in a worker thread. With a large history, the training and the scoring of a statement took seconds on the interface thread (about 0.4 s to train and 0.8 s to score 200 rows with 10 000 categorized rows, on test data), at each import and at each "＋" rule: the window froze. Now the rows show at once, "The app calculates the category suggestions…" tells that the suggestions come, and Save waits for them. A category picked or a name changed during the computation stays the choice of the user, also when the suggestions come while you type a name. A new computation (another file, a new rule) stops the older one: five quick "＋" clicks cost one computation, not five (#52).

releases.title: Stabilization
releases.summary: Stabilization release. A statement import is saved once and in one SQL transaction, the database has schema versions with a copy before each upgrade, and CI builds and publishes the app again: a Windows setup and portable ZIP, a Linux AppImage, .deb and archive. Also includes the Account Details pages and the documentation pass that started this version.

entries: `TODO.md` — standing backlog of known limitations, bugs, and cleanups found during a full file-by-file review, split out of what used to be `ARCHITECTURE.MD`'s "Known Limitations / TODOs" section.
`version.md` (this file) — top-level changelog, replacing the ad-hoc "Feature pass — ..." narrative headers that used to accumulate at the top of `ARCHITECTURE.MD`.
`tools/generate_docs.py` — writes a file and module listing, with the descriptions of the `@brief`-style header comments, to `docs/generated/source-tree.md`. CI does not run it.

**Account Details — balance chart time-range + Y-axis controls.** Time range presets (`7D` / `1M` / `6M` / `1Y` / `From start` / `Custom`, rolling from the account's own last transaction date, `Custom` via plain `yyyy-MM-dd` fields) plus a Y-axis scale toggle: "Auto" (existing tight-fit behavior) vs. "From 0" (pins the axis minimum to 0).

**Account Details — "Income by category" / "Expenses by category" pies.** Two new 2-level nested pie charts — category ring (inner) + subcategory ring (outer), each ring its own `PieSeries` in its own `GraphsView` stacked via `anchors.fill` (not Qt Graphs' native `PieSlice` sub-slice feature — turned out to render the opposite ring order needed; and not two `PieSeries` sharing one `GraphsView` either — that made `onClicked` stop firing on both rings). Both rings' slices show labels. A click on a slice is meant to show "Category —" / "Subcategory —" + amount + percentage, but the slices do not get clicks yet (#57). Income/expense is derived per-transaction from credit/debit, not a tag on `Category`. Backed by the new `AccountController::accountCategoryBreakdown(accountIndex)`.

**Category prediction on statement import** — imported rows now arrive with a suggested category/subcategory and a real confidence score, learned from the user's own already- categorized transactions. No trained model and nothing persisted but the user's rules: a four-rung cascade (user rule → exact merchant key → fuzzy key → TF-IDF k-NN over word tokens and character trigrams), plus sign gating and a monthly-recurrence boost. Confidence is calibrated to the review screen's existing badge thresholds — a merchant seen once scores 0.67 (amber), twice 0.80 (green) — and drops back automatically when the user recategorizes. New `src/predict/LabelNormalizer.{h,cpp}` (merchant-key normalization — the step most of the accuracy actually comes from) and `src/predict/CategoryPredictor.{h,cpp}`. Fulfils `PROJECT.md` § Category System — Prediction.

**`category_rules` table + `Data::CategoryRule`** — user-authored "always categorize labels like X as Y" rules, the top rung of the cascade and the fastest-learning path in the system (one click, permanent). `src/db/tables/CategoryRulesTable.{h,cpp}` plus `Database::loadCategoryRules()` / `addCategoryRule()` (upsert, so re-teaching replaces rather than stacks) / `removeCategoryRule()`. A category-only rule (no subcategory) saves correctly.

**Import review screen — RULE column and confidence tooltips.** A `＋` per row teaches a rule from that row's merchant key and current category, then re-scores the whole statement so every other row for the same merchant snaps to it immediately. Hovering the CONFIDENCE badge explains *why* the predictor picked that category ("Categorized "EDF" as Utilities in 3 of 3 previous transactions"). The line above the table is now a live "auto-filled N of M rows" summary (`SnapshotImportController::predictionInfo`) instead of the "no model exists yet" placeholder.

**`SnapshotImportController::evaluatePredictor()`** — leave-one-out accuracy of the predictor over the user's own categorized transactions (coverage, category/pair accuracy, mean confidence, per-rung breakdown), so the tuning constants can be checked against real data instead of argued about. Backed by `Predict::CategoryPredictor::evaluate()`.

**`TransactionsTable::allCategorized()` / `Database::allCategorizedTransactions()`** — every categorized transaction across every account, oldest first; the predictor's training set. Deliberately ignores account boundaries.

**`tools/predictor_selftest.cpp`** — sanity tests for `src/predict/`, covering normalization, each cascade rung, sign gating, recurrence, subcategory ambiguity and the evaluator. It runs with the other tests (`tests/CMakeLists.txt`, below).

Full CI/CD pipeline on GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, documented in `CI-CD.md`). Every pull request, and every push to `main`, `develop`, `release/**` and `hotfix/**`, builds and packages the app on Windows and Linux and runs the tests and linters as independent, individually re-runnable jobs. The project follows gitflow: merging a `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branch into `main` publishes a GitHub release and its tag, once every blocking job (including Tests and Changelog) is green, and CI then opens a pull request that merges `main` back into `develop`, opens the next version and starts CI on that pull request. Releases wait in a queue, one at a time, and a re-run of the release job finishes what an earlier run started without publishing twice. CI never commits to `main`. Ships a Windows setup (`.exe`, made with Inno Setup: it asks "for me only" or "for all users", and the setup of a newer version updates an installed copy in place) and portable `.zip`, a Linux `.AppImage`, `.deb` and portable `.tar.gz`, source archives and `SHA256SUMS.txt` — none of which need Qt installed on the target machine.

`version.json` + `tools/version.py` — the version and the changelog are now one machine-readable file. `CMakeLists.txt` reads `current` straight into `project(... VERSION ...)`, so the build, the installer file names, the release tag and the app's own `setApplicationVersion()` can no longer disagree. `version.md` is generated from it (`version.py render`); log a change with `version.py add <Section> "<text>"`. Only the current version can be in progress: `bump` renames an in-progress version instead of adding a second one, `add` refuses a released version, and `check --base origin/main` refuses any change to a version that is released on `main`.

Self-contained deployment via `qt_generate_deploy_qml_app_script()` — `cmake --install` now produces a directory that runs on a machine with no Qt, and every package is cut from that one tree. Plus `packaging/` (generated app icon, `.desktop` entry, AppStream metadata, AppImage and `.deb` build scripts) and `LICENSE` (MIT), which doubles as the setup's licence page. The QML module builds into `<build>/qml/FinanceDashboard/` (`QT_QML_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`), so it no longer takes the path of the Linux executable, which made the Linux link fail.

`tests/CMakeLists.txt` — CTest targets (`cmake -DFD_BUILD_TESTS=ON`, then `ctest`) that CI runs on every push: `predictor_selftest` (above), and the two Qt Test suites below. Partially clears `TODO.md`'s "no tests" item. `tests/import_save_test.cpp` (Qt Test) runs the statement-import save path end to end on a temporary database: rows without a category, subcategory or date, the reconciliation adjustment row, a category-only rule, a failed save and its retry. The app and the tests compile the same core sources (`FD_CORE_SOURCES`), and `cmake --build build --target fd_tests` builds every test. `tests/db_migration_test.cpp` (Qt Test) opens databases built the way older versions left them and checks each migration step.

**Docker build — build the app on any machine with only Docker installed.** `compose.yaml` + `.env` (options documented in `.env.example`: `TARGET` = `windows`/`linux`, `LINK_MODE` = `shared`/`static`, `BUILD_TYPE`, `QT_VERSION`, `LLVM_MINGW_VERSION`, job counts) + `docker/Dockerfile` (multi-stage toolchain image, one per target × link mode) + `docker/scripts/` (in-container build, packaging and static-Qt-from-source scripts) + `tools/docker-build.ps1`/`.sh` one-command wrappers. Windows is cross-compiled with llvm-mingw 17.0.6 (clang) against Qt's prebuilt `win64_llvm_mingw` 6.11.1; output goes to `dist/<target>-<mode>-<build type>/` (launcher + `app/` with exe + DLLs/plugins/qml for shared, a single executable for static). Build image is Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35, so Linux builds run on Ubuntu 22.04+/Debian 12+) with CMake from PyPI, and aqtinstall installed from a pinned master commit — the 3.3.0 release can't find Qt ≥ 6.11 Windows packages (Qt split the Windows repo per compiler: "Failed to locate XML data for Qt version '6.11.1'"), into a venv (`/opt/pytools`, with CMake) because 22.04's system pip builds it against the system setuptools 59 ("AttributeError: ignore_egg_info_in_manifest"). Static Qt sources fall back to download.qt.io's `archive/`. Also `qml/static-imports/StaticImports.qml` (static builds only: makes Qt link the Basic Controls style) and `.gitattributes` (LF for container scripts). Not yet run end-to-end. See `README.md` § Building with Docker.

**Docker build — pre-build requirement check.** `tools/check-requirements.ps1` / `.sh` (standalone, or run first by `tools/docker-build.*`): validates `.env`, Docker (installed, running, Linux containers, Compose v2, memory/disk sized for the link mode), that the Qt version / llvm-mingw release exist for the chosen target + link mode, that llvm-mingw's LLVM matches the one Qt's Windows binaries were built with (windows-shared only — static compiles Qt itself), and whether this computer can run the result (Windows build/CPU; Linux glibc/system libraries, fewer for static). New `.env` options `CHECK_REQUIREMENTS` and `FORCE_BUILD` (+ `-SkipChecks`/`-Force`, `--skip-checks`/`--force`).

**Docker build — timestamped run logs.** Every `tools/docker-build.*` run writes `logs/docker-build/<yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss>_<variant>/` with `summary.txt` (per-step result + duration), `env.txt`, `requirements.log`, `image.log`, `container.log`, and per-step `configure.log` / `build.log` / `deploy.log` from inside the container (`logs/` mounted at `/work/logs`, `RUN_LOG_DIR`). Logged output is decoded as UTF-8 and empty stderr lines no longer show up as "System.Management.Automation.RemoteException" in Windows PowerShell.

**Launcher.** The packages of the Docker build start through a launcher next to `app/`: `launcher/windows/main.cpp` (Win32, no Qt, statically linked — CMake target `FinanceDashboardLauncher`) and `launcher/linux/FinanceDashboard.sh`. It checks `app/requirements.txt` (generated by `deploy.py`: every packaged file, min Windows build, binaries to `ldd` on Linux), shows every requirement as OK/FAIL if something's wrong, and reports loader errors (missing DLL) the app itself can't. The packages that CI builds do not have it yet (#93).

**Start-up stage.** `src/startup/StartupChecks.h/.cpp`, run by `main.cpp` on every launch: requirement checks (none yet — placeholder for future ones) then initialization (data folder and database open, moved out of `main.cpp`). A failed fatal step (a database that does not open, see Fixed) loads the new `qml/StartupErrorWindow.qml` (every step as met / not met + fix hint) instead of `Main.qml`.

`CONTRIBUTING.md`, a pull-request template and issue forms (bug, feature, chore): the gitflow branch model (`main`, `develop`, `feature/*`, `bugfix/*`, `release/*`, `hotfix/*`), stacked pull requests (each one based on the one before it, merged from the bottom up), Conventional Commits, the label set, the definition of done and the repository settings. Dependabot pull requests now target `develop`.

**Database schema versioning.** `PRAGMA user_version` and ordered migration steps in `Database::upgrade()`, run when the app opens the database, all in one SQL transaction: the file is either upgraded or unchanged. Before it upgrades an existing database, and before any change to it, the app saves a copy next to it (`finance_dashboard.backup-<date>.db`, made with `VACUUM INTO`), and a dialog at start-up says what changed. A database from a newer version of the app, or an upgrade that fails, stops the app at start-up with the reason, and the file is not changed (the connection is closed, so nothing writes to it; a failed upgrade removes its copy). Migration 1 drops the `iban`, `bic` and `number` columns of an old `accounts` table and keeps its id counter; their values are also removed from the copy, and the file is compacted (`VACUUM`) so that no old bytes stay in it. Migration 2 adds the transaction fingerprints. `resetAll()` runs the steps again on the empty tables.
`README.md` rewritten to be a short, professional front door (what the app is, prerequisites, build/run steps).

**Account Details — transaction history table is now horizontally scrollable** instead of overflowing past the card's border on a narrow window: the header/row `Rectangle`s use a fixed `Layout.preferredWidth` and the table sits inside a `ScrollView`, which only shows a horizontal scrollbar when the card is narrower than the table.

**Account Details — all five `GraphsView`s (balance chart + both pies' inner/outer rings) use an explicit, higher-contrast `GraphsTheme`** instead of `ColorScheme.Dark` defaults, which read as too washed-out against this app's near-black cards — the same Catppuccin Mocha colors as the rest of the app.

**`HoverPoint.qml`'s hover hit-box enlarged (26×26 → 34×34), and its tooltip now flips below/clamps horizontally instead of always centering above the point** — the small hit-box made hovering hard to land, and always-above-centered positioning cropped the tooltip for any point near the chart's top edge or a side. Both are shared-component fixes, so they apply to every page's line-chart hover (Account Details, Savings, Cash Flow, Investments, Overview, Projects).

**Confidence badge bucketing/formatting moved from QML to C++** — `Fmt::confidenceVariant()` / `Fmt::confidenceText()` (`src/utils/Formatter.h`) replace `ImportSnapshotPage.qml`'s page-level `confidenceVariant()`/`confidenceText()` JS helpers; rows now carry ready-to-display `confidenceText`/`confidenceVariant` alongside the raw `confidence`, matching the app's "values arrive pre-formatted from the controller" convention. Clears the corresponding `TODO.md` § Convention drift item, and keeps the 0.5/0.8 thresholds next to the predictor that produces the numbers.

**`Data::ImportedTransaction` gained `predictionReason`** — one line of plain English explaining where the suggested category came from, shown as a tooltip on the confidence badge. Review-screen-only and never persisted, same status as `confidence`.

Both packaging jobs smoke-test the app before publishing: the Windows build is launched from its install tree with the real `windows` platform plugin (the tree has no `offscreen` plugin) and its setup is installed, installed again over itself and uninstalled in both install modes, the Linux `.AppImage` under Xvfb with the real `xcb` plugin, each with the builder's own Qt removed from the environment so a package that only works on the build machine fails the job. The `.deb` is installed and started in a clean `ubuntu:24.04` container (`packaging/linux/test-deb.sh`), which checks its `Depends` line: `make-deb.sh` now computes it from the `NEEDED` entries of the files the app loads (the system libraries that the bundled Qt needs: X11/xcb, Wayland, OpenGL/EGL, fonts, D-Bus, GLib) and stops with an error that names the library when one is missing or no package owns it, so the package no longer fails with "could not load the Qt platform plugin xcb" on a machine without them.
`cmake_minimum_required` 3.20 → 3.21 (Qt's CMake deployment API), and `main.cpp` takes its version from the `FD_VERSION_STRING` compile definition instead of a hard-coded `"0.2.0"`.

**Account Details — the 3 KPI cards (Current balance / Transactions / Type-Category) are now exactly equal width and height.** Width: `Layout.fillWidth: true` alone left the middle card a hair narrower than its neighbors (QtQuick Layouts' leftover-pixel remainder handling wasn't symmetric); all three now bind an explicit, identical `Layout.preferredWidth`. Height: the Transactions card's empty `sub` line made QtQuick Layouts exclude it from the card's implicit-height calculation (a hair shorter than its two neighbors, which both have a real sub line) — now shows "All time" instead of an empty string.

**Statement import — saving works for rows without a category, subcategory or date, and a failed save writes nothing.** A null `QString` was bound as SQL `NULL` in `TEXT NOT NULL` columns, so the save failed on a first import (no predicted category), a category without a subcategory, the reconciliation adjustment row and a cleared date in the transaction editor; text and dates are now bound as `''` (`Sql::text()`, `src/db/tables/SqlText.h`). The rows, the account link and the balance checkpoints of an import now go in one SQL transaction (`Database::saveImport()`). Before, the rows written before a failing one stayed in the database, and each retry stored them again.

**Statement import — a statement row is saved only once.** Re-importing a statement, or importing one that overlaps an earlier one, saved every row again while the reconciliation stayed green. Each row now has a fingerprint, unique per account: the bank's reference (the last exact "Internal ref.:" label of the description) and the amount when the row has one, so that a later export with another value date or running balance still matches, else the dates, debit, credit and balance after in cents, and the description. Rows that the account already has are skipped, and the status line and the import report say how many. A skipped row with the reference and amount of a saved row but another operation date (the bank may reuse its references) is counted in the import report and the upgrade dialog, with a link to issue #126. Two identical rows of one statement are two transactions (the second one has its occurrence number in its fingerprint), and a row that breaks a `NOT NULL` column fails the save instead of being skipped. The upgrade to schema version 2 removes the duplicates that earlier re-imports saved, after it saves a copy of the database: of each row, the copy with a category stays, then the one with a subcategory, then the oldest one. The upgrade dialog says how many removed copies had another category, label, date or balance, and the application log lists them.

**A database that does not open stops the app with the cause.** `Database::open()` used to leave the connection open after a failure, so the app started on an empty dashboard and the SQLite error went only to the log. It now closes the connection, and the start-up error window shows the cause ("file is not a database", for example) and what to do.

**Statement import — row dates get the right year.** A row date has no year (`MM/dd`); it used to get the year of the period start, so a January row of a December → January statement was dated a year too early, and a December row of a January statement eleven months later. It now gets the year that puts it in the statement period (from 31 days before its start to its end), and a statement without a readable "Period" line is refused instead of losing every row (#30). When a period of 11 months or more lets a date fit two years, the later one is used, with a warning; a row date that cannot be placed is logged. A 29 February row is no longer skipped (#31). Rows that an earlier version saved with a wrong year are not corrected: a re-import of their statement adds the row with the right date, and the old row must be deleted by hand.

**Statement import — amounts.** Amounts grouped with spaces ("1 300.00", also with no-break spaces), with a decimal comma ("1 234,56 €") or with a thousands comma ("1,234") are read, and "nan", "inf", garbled grouping ("1.2.3", "0,123") or any text that is not a number are refused: a debit of "-1 300.00" used to skip its row with only a warning (#32). An amount that an earlier version read wrong ("1,234" as 1.234) is not corrected: a re-import adds the right row next to the old one.
See `Added`/`Changed`/`Fixed` above.

`README.md` — new "Building with Docker" section (quick start, requirement check, run logs, output layout) and `docker/` + `launcher/` in the project layout. `ARCHITECTURE.MD` — build-system row and index rows for the Docker build and the start-up stage.

releases.title: Baseline
releases.summary: Starting point for this changelog. Everything below was already built before `version.md` existed; recorded here as one baseline entry rather than reconstructed commit-by-commit. Matches `CMakeLists.txt`'s `project(... VERSION 0.2.0 ...)` at the time this file was introduced.

groups.title: Navigation & shell
entries: `Main.qml` app shell: collapsible left sidebar (`SidebarCategory.qml`) + `StackLayout`, driven by a single `currentViewId` source of truth. "ADMIN" section divider above Account Management / Database Management.

Shared QML component library: `PageHeader`, `PillButton`, `GhostButton`, `StatusBadge`, `FormRow`, `ColorPickerRow`, `FormDialog`, `ConfirmDialog`, `EmptyState`, `ColumnHeaderCell`, `KpiCard`, `ChartCard`, `SidebarCategory`, `ColorComboBox`.

groups.title: Analytics pages (UI pass, mock data)
entries: Overview (net worth KPIs, stacked area by account type, allocation donut, monthly net-change bars), Cash Flow (income/expense bars, rolling average, category donut/stacked bars, biggest expenses), Savings (balance lines, ceiling/goal progress, yearly interest), Investments (portfolio vs. deposits, allocation, monthly performance), Projects (goal tracking + a real C++ annuity-math loan simulator). All five still serve `[MOCK]` data pending DB wiring.

groups.title: Transactions
entries: Statement import wizard (`ImportSnapshotPage.qml` / `SnapshotImportController`): real CSV parsing (`SumeriaCcpCsvExtractionTemplate`), editable/categorizable review table with resizable + persisted columns, account auto-match by stored hash fingerprint, parse log popup, real save to the `transactions` table.

Import report + reconciliation: post-save report (income/expense/net, category/subcategory breakdown with a pie chart), two-check balance reconciliation against declared statement balances, a mismatch-resolution dialog (review kept rows / add an adjustment transaction).
Auto-remembered balance checkpoints from every statement's declared start/end balance.
Categories & Subcategories management (add/rename/recolor/remove, SQLite-backed).
View & Edit Transactions: full per-account transaction table with colored category/ subcategory badges and an edit modal.

groups.title: Accounts & admin
entries: Manage Accounts: add/edit/remove accounts (name/type/category/currency/notes — no IBAN/BIC/account number stored), per-account hash-fingerprint management, per-account balance-checkpoint management, a routed per-account transactions view.
Account types & categories management (SQLite-backed CRUD).
Account History: read-only per-account view (current balance, balance-over-time line chart computed by replaying transactions, transaction list).
Database Management: whole-database reset (empty or reseeded with mock data) and per-account cleanup (clear transactions / delete account), all behind confirmation dialogs.

groups.title: Data layer
entries: SQLite persistence (`Database` singleton + one table class per table) for categories, subcategories, accounts, account hashes, account categories, account types, transactions, and balance checkpoints.
HMAC-SHA256 account-hash fingerprinting (`AccountHashing.h`), shared between import matching and manual account linking.

groups.title: Tooling
entries: clang-tidy (build-time opt-in + on-demand script) and qmllint (auto-wired via `qt_add_qml_module`) static analysis, plus `tools/run-static-analysis.ps1` to run both and log to `logs/`.

The original Qt Widgets app and the intermediate ported-but-unwired QML generation (`AnalyticsController`, `EntryController`, the legacy `DatabaseController`, `OverviewController`, `PortfolioController`, the legacy `ImportController`, `qml/tabs/*`) — deleted outright once nothing referenced them; recoverable from git history before this baseline if ever needed again.
Keyword-based category auto-suggestion (`CategoryKeywords.h`) — replaced by the user-managed category list.
`iban`/`bic`/`number` columns on the `accounts` table — dropped for security; accounts are now matched only via stored hash fingerprints.
